CHIEF COMPLAINT
Chest pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a new patient referred from the ER with a history of chest pain that occurred in early October 2020. She experienced sharp, central chest pain located behind the breastbone for four days, which she initially tolerated but eventually required emergency room evaluation due to inability to relieve the pain. The pain was worse with eating. She also noted associated difficulty swallowing during this period. The ER workup included EKG and blood tests, all normal, with normal cardiac workup. The chest pain and swallowing difficulty resolved approximately three days after the ER visit. She has been asymptomatic for the three months since the initial episode. Patient notes she was experiencing a stressful job transition at the time of symptom onset. She has not had any heartburn or indigestion that she is aware of, though she is unsure what heartburn typically feels like.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies abdominal pain. Bowel movements are normal. Denies family history of GI problems.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Uterine fibroids, anemia, cholecystectomy (several years ago)

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
No known family history of GI problems.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports currently attempting to lose weight. Recent stressful job transition in early October 2020.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Abdomen soft. Mild tenderness to light palpation in upper abdominal quadrants, symmetric. No tenderness to palpation in lower abdomen. Otherwise normal exam.

RESULTS
Prior ER workup: normal EKG and blood tests with normal cardiac workup.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Chest pain, resolved. Differential diagnosis includes GERD, dyspepsia, esophagitis, musculoskeletal etiologies, and anxiety. Likely etiology is anxiety related to job transition with possible musculoskeletal contribution. Discussed EGD versus monitoring. Patient elected to self-monitor symptoms and will call office if any recurrence or change occurs. Will proceed with watchful waiting rather than immediate endoscopy given three-month asymptomatic period. Follow up as needed for any additional GI complaints.
